title: Waiting on you (C): Home placement stays consistent when the Waiting set changes (spike-gated)
description:
Session **C** of LIN-4144 (Home's Waiting on you live refresh). This is plan piece 5: Home stays consistent when the Waiting set changes. It lands after B (LIN-4242: fragment, merge, tick).

## This piece's slice of the approved plan

**Problem:** placement is the server view's job. In `buildHomeView` (`lib/home-view.js`, `lib/home-pipeline.js`), a waiting task leaves Running, Up next and recent, and an answered one returns. If only the Waiting section repaints, a new ruling's task shows twice and one answered elsewhere leaves its task nowhere (LIN-4117 reachability).

**Implemented (plan section pruned at close-out).** The approach, spike gate and testing sections were discharged by the landed work. The spike went GO and the swap shipped, not the "Home changed — reload" fallback; the plan was implemented as approved, with these deviations: `init()` binds no rows (delegation and lazy mount), so the swap merges fresh `rowData`, destroys old mounted PromptSections, replays expanded state scoped to the new rows, and defers on an opened task, a card holding input, a field in focus, a dispatch in flight, an opened "show N more" list, or a search. PR: [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2282](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2282>) (squash commit `172f644a`). The full pre-prune description is in the task snapshots, and the plan, spike result and review are in the comment trail (spike `0c5cb84c`, review `5698c1b4`).

**Out of scope:** a Home-wide live repaint beyond this, and a reduction shared by the badge and Home.

**Session fit: fits one session.** It is one change-triggered swap behind a spike gate, with a defined fallback if the spike fails.

**Grounding commit:** LinearViewer `main` at `476d9ad478ede67da5cb44195ce24c98d07afa61` (the plan and its review were both written against it; re-checked unchanged at breakdown, 4 Nov 22:40Z).

**Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4144's approving plan-review (comment** `7ad6c803-0434-496e-b1aa-0a9d7d36f0ab`**, rev 1).**

**Starting point:** LIN-4144's approved plan is where this piece starts. Read it in full in LIN-4144's description (`## Implementation Plan`), and read the review's 11 builder notes in comment `7ad6c803`. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4144.

parent.title: Home's Waiting on you has no live refresh: cards and count go stale until reload

comments.body: Unblocked: LIN-4242 (B) is merged and deployed (ee8ec42e). Today only the count line's "N waiting on you" part follows the live refresh; Running, Up next and the count line's other parts still reflect the set at load, which is this ticket's scope. `public/llms.txt` (waiting-on-you) states that limit and should be updated when this lands.

## Spike result: **GO, with conditions.** Ship the swap, not the "Home changed — reload" fallback.

**Question:** after a Waiting key-set change, can Running and Up next be swapped from one Home document read, with rows re-bound once (no double-binding) and the reader's fold state kept?
**Yes would look like:** a real-server E2E where one click opens a swapped row once, its opened task mounts once, a collapsed desk section stays collapsed, persisted expanded rows reopen as a reload would, and an unchanged set reads nothing. **No would look like:** any double toggle or double mount, or fold state lost.
**Result:** yes, on all counts. The tests fail with the swap disabled.

### The problem is not where the ticket put it
The ticket says "`init()` binds from page-carried `rowData`". That is not how rows are bound at `ee8ec42e`. `init()` binds no row. Expand, collapse and keyboard are **delegated on `document`** (`public/app.js` `init()`). The opened task mounts **lazily** from `rowData` when its details load (`mountHomePromptSections`, guarded by `data-mounted`). Folds bind once (`bindHomeFolds`, guarded by `data-bound`). So double-binding cannot happen unless someone calls `init()` again, and the swap never does. The real risks were elsewhere, and the spike handles each one:
1. **Sections come and go.** `renderRunningSection`/`renderUpNextSection` return `''` when empty. A swap has to insert or remove a whole section. Insertion anchors are captured at startup: the search-results element, then Running.
2. **Desk collapse and search hiding live on the section element.** The spike keeps the section wrapper and header and replaces only `.running-body`/`.up-next-body`. A section new to the page takes the persisted `runningCollapsed`/`upNextCollapsed`.
3. **Old rows hold mounted PromptSections**, even when collapsed. `destroyHomePromptSections(old)` runs before the replace.
4. **`state.expanded` must reach the new rows.** `applyState` is page-wide (`resetDOM`), so the spike replays the expanded pass **scoped to the new section** only. The result is the same as a reload.
5. **Fresh `rowData`/`topTaskId`** come from the fetched document's `__HOME_PROMPT_OPTS__` JSON block and are merged before any new row mounts.
6. **A false blocker found by the test:** a clicked row keeps focus (`tabindex=0`). "Focus in the region" therefore deferred the swap forever. Only focus in a field (input, textarea, select, contenteditable) now counts.

### What I built (branch `spike/lin-4243-placement-swap`, commit `12ea626d`, not landed)
`createHomePlacement` in `public/app.js`, about 170 lines, called from B's `loadWaiting` after `mergeWaitingCards`:
- It compares the merged body's ruling keys (via B's `rulingKeyOf`) with the set the desk was last placed for.
- It **defers** while Running/Up next has an opened task (`.details:not(.hidden)`), a card that `cardHoldsInput` (including cards in collapsed tasks), focus in a field, an opened "show N more" fold (`.home-fetched`), or an active search. It says so once in `home-desk-live`.
- Otherwise it does **one** `fetch(location.pathname + location.search)`, parses with `DOMParser`, swaps both bodies and the count line's parts into B's persistent wrapper, then `setWaitingCount` from the merged cards.
- `placedKeys` advances to the merged set on read, so a page/fragment disagreement can never cause a read on every tick.
- Everything is captured at startup in `initWaitingOnYou`. There are no page-wide lookups per tick.

### Evidence
- `tests/e2e/lin-4243-placement-swap.spec.js`, real server and local harness, 3 tests, **3 passed**:
  1. A ruling on a Running task: the task shows in Waiting only, the count line changes, and there is exactly 1 Home read (request-counted). Two more ticks: still 1 read. Answered in another tab: back in Running/Up next, 2 reads.
  2. An opened task in Up next: the swap is deferred, the live region says "Home changed…", and there are 0 reads over two ticks. After the task is closed, the next tick swaps.
  3. Running collapsed, and an Up next task opened then closed (mounted, hidden), before the swap. After the swap: Running is still collapsed (▶), the old mount is gone, and one click opens the task (`aria-expanded=true`) with exactly one mounted PromptSection reading fresh `rowData`. A second click closes it. A persisted `state.expanded` entry reopens its row on the next swap, as a reload does.
- **Witness:** with `check()` forced to `'same'`, all 3 fail.
- **No regressions:** `lin-4114-waiting-on-you` + `lin-4242-waiting-live` + this spec = **24/24 passed**. Unit tests `no-page-wide-label-listener`, `lin-4114-owner-gate`, `lin-4114-inflight-lock`, `lin-4113-home-desk`, `lin-4242-waiting-live`, `lin-4242-waiting-merge` = **85/85 passed**. The full suite and CI have not been run on the branch.

### Conditions for the build
- **Run in flight in a collapsed opened task.** A dispatch pressed and still pending would be destroyed by the swap. Add an in-flight check to the blocker (or confirm `PromptSection.destroy` handles it) before shipping. **Not tested.**
- **An opened "show N more"** (recent) defers the swap until it is gone, which in practice means until reload. The alternative is to swap and re-fetch the fold. I chose defer to keep fold state. Decide at build.
- **The deferral notice is screen-reader only** (`home-desk-live` is `sr-only`), as the plan says. A sighted reader sees nothing while it is deferred. Consider a visible cue.
- **A persisted expanded row reopens on swap** (same as reload). That is correct, but a reader may not expect it.
- **Cost:** one full Home render (`gatherHomeInputs`) per key-set change per open owner tab, the same as a reload. Not timed on `tests/perf/lin-4024-home-shape.spec.js`.
- Build-time tidy: drop the `window.__homePlacement` hook or make it test-only, add a unit test for `blockedBy`, and replace B's interim `public/llms.txt` line with the live behaviour.

### Still unknown
- The typed-text-in-a-collapsed-task's card path is covered by code but has no test.
- No behaviour seen against a large Home (paged recent, many projects).
- The full CI suite has not been run on the branch.

PR (ready for review, CI green): https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2282

Home's Running and Up next now follow a change of the Waiting key set. One Home read per change (none on an unchanged tick); the swap replaces both bodies and the count line's parts; the swap waits, announced once in home-desk-live, while the reader has a task open there, a card holding typed text or focus, a dispatch in flight, or a search.

Evidence (commit 9c235244): Unit suite 23,197 pass / 0 fail; hermetic keyed arm clean; new policy unit tests 17/17 (mutation witnesses fail 3 and 2 as expected). E2E: LIN-4243 spec 3/3 pass, and 3/3 fail with the swap disabled; lin-4114/4242/4243 24/24; Home and dispatch specs 387 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing). PR CI: unit, all four E2E shards, secret scan and CI success all pass.

Named limits: an opened "show N more" list defers the swap until reload (announced; llms.txt states it). Not covered by tests: typed text in a question card inside a closed opened task (unit only), the in-flight dispatch counter (unit only via the policy), and large-Home timing.

## Review — LIN-4243

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2282, head `9c235244`. The base is `main` = `ee8ec42e` (LIN-4242), and `main` has not moved since.

CI: green on `9c235244`: unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, secret scan and the overall CI check all pass. I also re-ran the new tests myself on that head: the unit file passed 17/17 and the E2E spec 3/3.

### Scope against the plan
The PR follows the approved route: the spike went GO, it is recorded on LIN-4144 (comment of 01:54Z), and the swap shipped, not the fallback. The change stays inside the planned places: `public/app.js` (`createDeskPlacement`), a new `public/home-placement.js` (the policy), `public/common.js` (counts dispatches in flight), `lib/render.js` (loads the script), `public/llms.txt` and the source map. The spike's build conditions are all handled:
- **Dispatch in flight:** handled. `window.dispatchPrompt` is wrapped, and every caller reaches it late-bound (prompt-section.js:1692/1747/2403, app.js:1617, close-out.js).
- **Opened "show N more" list:** the swap waits, the reader is told, and llms.txt names this limit.
- **`blockedBy` unit test:** added.
- **B's interim llms.txt line:** replaced with the live behaviour.
- **`window.__homePlacement` hook:** dropped.

I found no correctness defect in the swap. Each piece checks out:
- **Body-only replace:** the section wrappers and headers stay, so a collapsed section stays collapsed and search hiding survives.
- **Inserting or removing a whole section:** the anchors (the search results, then Running) match the order `lib/render.js` draws.
- **Count line:** its `hidden` class is reset by `setWaitingCount`.
- **`placed`:** it advances only after a successful swap. A failed read is retried on the next tick, which is deliberate and unit-tested.

**Regression check:** `git log` on the touched files shows LIN-4242, LIN-4241, LIN-4105 (desk order in llms.txt) and LIN-4114 (a task appears once). None of them is undone. The section order in llms.txt is kept.

**Isolated, or one of a class:** one more opened list exists. A "more-of-parent" fold puts its rows straight into the tree, not in a `.home-fetched` wrapper, so `openFold` misses it. But opening it requires an expanded parent. That parent has a `.details` wrapper whenever `issue.url` is set, which is effectively always, so `openedTask` already makes the swap wait. I treat this as handled and record nothing for it.

### Mutation check (each reverted afterwards)
| Mutation | Unit (17) | E2E (3) |
|---|---|---|
| Drop `replayExpanded(el)` | — | **1 failed** ✓ |
| Replace the whole section instead of its body | — | **1 failed** ✓ |
| Drop `destroyHomePromptSections(old)` | — | **3 passed ✗** |
| Drop the fresh `rowData` merge in `apply` | — | **3 passed ✗** |
| `sectionFacts`: `cardHoldsInput: false` | 17 pass ✗ | 3 passed ✗ |
| `sectionFacts`: `openFold: false` | 17 pass ✗ | 3 passed ✗ |
| `sectionFacts`: `fieldFocused: false` | 17 pass ✗ | 3 passed ✗ |

The PR's "mutation witnesses" hold only for the pure policy, where `blockedBy` is given ready-made facts. No test reaches the DOM side. Three claims the PR and comments make are untested:
- "the old rows' mounted opened tasks are destroyed": E2E test 3 checks only that `[data-mounted]` is gone, which a detached node satisfies anyway.
- "reads fresh `rowData`": LOCAL-T's `rowData` was already on the page at load.
- typed text, focus or an opened list makes the swap wait: `sectionFacts` has no test.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **[inside — the ticket's witness 7, "nothing is double-bound / opened task mounts once"] The old PromptSection is torn down before the swap.** *Before the merge:* in `tests/e2e/lin-4243-placement-swap.spec.js` test 3, before `seedRuling`, record a destroy call on LOCAL-T's handle: `page.evaluate(() => { const el = document.querySelector('[data-testid="home-up-next-section"] [data-prompt-mount][data-mounted="true"]'); const d = el._promptSectionHandle.destroy; window.__destroyed = 0; el._promptSectionHandle.destroy = () => { window.__destroyed++; d(); }; })`. After the swap, assert `window.__destroyed === 1`. To confirm the test is a real witness, delete `if (old) destroyHomePromptSections(old)` in `public/app.js` `swapSection` and check the test goes red.
- **[inside — Approach: "merged before any new row mounts"] A row swapped in mounts with the fresh `rowData`.** *Before the merge:* in test 3, before the first swap, run `delete window.__HOME_PROMPT_OPTS__.rowData[<LOCAL-T's data-node-key>]`. Keep the existing `hasRowData === true` assertion after the swap. To confirm, delete the `page.rowData = {...}` merge in `apply` and check the test goes red.
- **[inside — Approach: "only when nothing there holds input"] The DOM facts that make the swap wait (`cardHoldsInput`, `fieldFocused`, `openFold`, `openedTask`).** *Before the merge:* add a `sectionFacts` block to `tests/unit/lin-4243-placement.test.js`. Use stub elements (`querySelector`, `querySelectorAll` and `contains` stubs, plus an active element with `matches`) so each fact turns true from its own selector or callback, and a focused `tabindex=0` row (not a field) reads `fieldFocused: false`. Each of the four mutations above must turn it red. The one place this protects that the opened-task check cannot: **typed text in a question card inside an opened task that was then closed** (`.details.hidden`, card still mounted). Optionally, a manual check on a live owner Home: type in such a card, close the row, raise a ruling elsewhere, and confirm the text survives and `home-desk-live` says "…answer you are typing…".
- **[inside — the named limit in llms.txt] An opened "show N more" list makes the swap wait, and the reader is told.** It is covered by the `sectionFacts` unit test above. No E2E is needed: seeding more than 10 recent rows costs more than the claim is worth.
- **[outside — a cost the plan accepted] One full Home render per change of the Waiting set, per open owner tab.** It has not been timed against a large Home (`tests/perf/lin-4024-home-shape.spec.js`). *Monitor:* server response time for `GET /workspace/:urlKey/` with `Accept: text/html` on the owner workspaces after the deploy. Only real Home sizes and real ruling rates show this cost. If it is high, close-out files a follow-up stating the problem on its own terms.
- **[inside — the ticket's witness 7] The two-tab owner flow in production** (raise a ruling, the task leaves Running; answer it in another tab, the task returns). *After the deploy:* a manual check on the owner's Home, as LIN-4242's close-out left one. It needs an owner sign-in, which this session does not have.

**Rollback:** revert the single squash commit for PR #2282. Nothing is persisted and no migration runs, so the change is fully reversible.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The swap is correct and follows the approved spike, and CI is green. Close-out must first add the three test strengthenings above (the destroy spy and the `rowData` delete in E2E test 3, and the `sectionFacts` unit block) and confirm each goes red under its mutation. These are test-only fixes and change no behaviour.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why difficult.** Only moderately. The server side was already right; the change bound in the page's binding model. The spike had done the hard part: it found that rows are delegated and lazily mounted, not bound by `init()`. What I still had to push through: `app.js` has no module boundary, so testing `blockedBy` meant pulling the policy out into `public/home-placement.js`. A PromptSection exposes no "busy" state, so a dispatch in flight was invisible, and I wrapped `dispatchPrompt` in `common.js` to count them. And the typed-text-in-a-closed-task path could not be seeded end to end, because an opened Up next row does not repaint a question card after a ruling is raised.

**2. What first.** Check two things before writing any code. Does the opened task repaint a question card after a ruling? (No, so that E2E was never reachable.) Does PromptSection have any in-flight signal? (No.) Both answers changed what I built; I learned them late.

**3. What I'd tidy.** `replayExpanded` copies `applyState`'s expanded pass. `applyState` should take a root, so there is one replay. The dispatch counter is a wrapper around `window.dispatchPrompt`; it belongs inside `dispatchPrompt` itself. Where a new section is inserted (after search results, else at the top of `main`) repeats `render.js`'s section order in a second place. An opened "show N more" defers the swap until reload — a real limit.

**4. The ticket, in a codebase I'd want.** "Add Running and Up next to the `home-waiting` fragment and swap them." That means a server fragment drawn by the same function as the page, the same pattern B used, and a scoped `applyState`. No spike, no `DOMParser` over the whole page, no gate.

**5. What the ticket got wrong.** The spike already corrected the main thing: "`init()` binds from rowData". The plan framed the gate as swap-or-reload-notice. In practice the swap still needs a reload-style message in one case (an opened fold), so the two outcomes were not as separate as written. It also did not anticipate a dispatch in flight or opened folds as blockers.

**6. What it left behind.**
- `public/home-placement.js` is a new, small module with a clear home. It sits beside `question-cards.js` as a second client policy module.
- The expanded-state replay now lives in two places.
- `window.dispatchesInFlight` is a new global with one reader.
- `DESK_SECTIONS` gained `section` and `placed` fields.
- The biggest change: Home's rendered HTML is now an input the client parses. The selectors the swap reads (`.running-body`, `in-progress-count`, `__HOME_PROMPT_OPTS__`) are now a contract with `render.js`, and only E2E guards it.
- Nothing got simpler.

**7. Did the larger scope pay?** In this task, yes. The spike had retired the binding risk, so building the swap was mostly tidying, and the reader gets correct placement rather than a reload notice. The costs: about 250 lines, one full Home render per key-set change per open owner tab, and two new deferral cases, one of them with its own named limit. I don't know what the Survey recommended. From what I saw, I'd draw the line where it landed: ship the swap for the common case, defer anything the reader has open, and leave fold replay and a desk fragment as follow-ups rather than growing this one.

## Close-out — LIN-4243

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2282, squash commit `172f644a`, pinned to head `19c1d258` (`--match-head-commit`). **Deployed:** harbour.cat footer shows `172f644`, and it serves `/home-placement.js` and an `app.js` with `createDeskPlacement`.

### Changes I made after the approval (test-only, no behaviour change), commit `19c1d258`
Each answers a "What CI Did Not Prove" line in review `5698c1b4`.
1. **Old PromptSection torn down (review: the destroy spy).** E2E test 3 in `tests/e2e/lin-4243-placement-swap.spec.js` spies on the old row's `destroy()` and asserts exactly 1 call after the swap. Mutation: drop `if (old) destroyHomePromptSections(old)` in `swapSection` → test 3 **fails** (Expected 1, Received 0).
2. **Swapped-in row mounts with fresh `rowData` (review: the `rowData` delete).** The test deletes LOCAL-T's `rowData` entry before the swap, and the existing `hasRowData === true` assertion now holds only if the swap's merge restored it. I also assert the mounted node key matches. Mutation: drop the `page.rowData = {...}` merge in `apply` → test 3 **fails** (Expected true, Received false).
3. **`sectionFacts` blocker facts (review: the unit block).** New `describe('sectionFacts…')` in `tests/unit/lin-4243-placement.test.js` (6 tests, stub elements). It includes a card holding typed text in a closed task (`openedTask: false`, `cardHoldsInput: true`, `blockedBy` → `input`) and a focused `tabindex=0` row (`fieldFocused: false`). Mutations `openedTask`, `openFold`, `fieldFocused` and `cardHoldsInput` forced to `false` each turn the file **red** (1, 1, 2 and 1 failures). All mutations were reverted.

### Ledger
- **Old PromptSection torn down (inside):** settled by change 1, with the mutation witness.
- **Fresh `rowData` before mount (inside):** settled by change 2, with the mutation witness.
- **DOM facts that make the swap wait, including typed text in a closed task (inside):** settled by change 3. Review accepted the `show N more` limit as covered by the unit test, so no E2E was added.
- **Cost of one full Home render per Waiting-set change per owner tab (outside):** not timed on a large Home. Named monitor from review: *server response time for `GET /workspace/:urlKey/` with `Accept: text/html` on the owner workspaces after the deploy.* If it runs high, a follow-up is to be filed on its own terms. No ticket filed now: nothing shows a problem, and a ticket would not fire. I cannot arm that monitor from here.
- **Two-tab owner flow in production (inside, post-deploy): NOT RUN.** It needs an owner sign-in, which this session does not have. For the operator: on the owner's Home, raise a ruling for a task shown in Running → the task leaves Running and shows in Waiting only; answer it in another tab → the task returns to Running/Up next; type in a question card inside a closed task, raise a ruling elsewhere, and confirm the text survives and `home-desk-live` says "…answer you are typing…". Recorded on the PR too.
- **Rollback (named by review):** revert the single squash commit `172f644a`. Nothing is persisted and no migration runs.

### CI
CI exists (`.github/workflows`, "Tests"). On head `19c1d258`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and CI success all **SUCCESS** (run 41957080349), read fresh before the merge. Main's run on the merge commit (41958084483) also **success**. Locally: unit suite 23,203 pass / 0 fail; the LIN-4243 E2E spec 3/3.

### Housekeeping
Description archived (snapshot confirmed in `/snapshots`, captured 03:03:38Z) and pruned: the Approach / Spike / Testing sections are replaced by a stub with the PR link and the deviations. The Problem, Out of scope, Session fit, Plan-review and Grounding lines are kept. No follow-up tickets were needed (the only outside item is conditional on the monitor). No related ticket to close: LIN-4241 and LIN-4242 are already Done, and LIN-4144 stays open for the owner's two-tab check.

issue.title: Waiting on you (B): live section — home-waiting fragment, shared keyed card merge, one rulings tick
